```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
if (!requireNamespace("forecast", quietly = TRUE)) stop("Install package 'forecast'.")
```

# 1. Settings

```{r settings}
fit_start <- as.Date("2015-01-01")   # first date used for fitting
h         <- 16L                     # forecast horizon (days), as in the competition
origin    <- as.Date("2017-07-30")   # last training day; the next 16 days are held out
pools     <- c("series", "family", "global")
cache     <- "holdout_results.rds"   # saved results; delete after changing model code
```

The models are fitted on data up to July 30, 2017 and forecast July 31 to
August 15, the last 16 days of the training data.

# 2. Data import

Same loading step and object names as `storesales.rmd`.

```{r read-data}
data_dir <- Sys.getenv("STORE_SALES_DATA", "store-sales-time-series-forecasting")
if (!dir.exists(data_dir)) stop("Knit from the Kaggle folder containing the data directory.")
csv_files <- sort(list.files(data_dir, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE))
datasets <- setNames(lapply(csv_files, function(path) {
  x <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if ("date" %in% names(x)) x$date <- as.Date(x$date)
  x
}), tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(csv_files)))
required <- c("train", "test", "stores", "oil", "holidays_events",
              "transactions", "sample_submission")
stopifnot(all(required %in% names(datasets)))
train <- datasets$train; test <- datasets$test; stores <- datasets$stores
holidays_events <- datasets$holidays_events
```

# 3. Features

`make_holiday_calendar` and `make_features` are copied unchanged from
`storesales.rmd`. When the files are merged, delete this chunk.

```{r partner-feature-functions}
make_holiday_calendar <- function(stores, events, dates) {
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(stores$store_nbr))
  out <- expand.grid(date = dates, store_nbr = stores$store_nbr)
  out$date <- as.Date(out$date, origin = "1970-01-01")
  out$holiday <- 0L; out$workday <- 0L
  eligible <- !is.na(events$transferred) &
    tolower(as.character(events$transferred)) == "false"
  e <- events[eligible & events$type %in%
    c("Holiday", "Transfer", "Additional", "Bridge", "Work Day"), ]
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(e))) {
    st <- switch(e$locale[i], National = stores$store_nbr,
      Regional = stores$store_nbr[stores$state == e$locale_name[i]],
      Local = stores$store_nbr[stores$city == e$locale_name[i]], integer())
    ix <- out$date == e$date[i] & out$store_nbr %in% st
    field <- if (e$type[i] == "Work Day") "workday" else "holiday"
    out[[field]][ix] <- 1L
  }
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(paste(out$date, out$store_nbr)))
  out
}

make_features <- function(date, promotion, holiday, workday) {
  time <- as.numeric(date - as.Date("2013-01-01"))
  x <- data.frame(trend = time / 365.25,
    weekday = factor((as.integer(date) + 3L) %% 7L + 1L, levels = 1:7),
    promo = log1p(promotion), holiday = holiday, workday = workday,
    payday15 = as.integer(format(date, "%d") == "15"),
    payday_end = as.integer(format(date + 1L, "%m") != format(date, "%m")))
  for (k in 1:3) {
    suffix <- if (k == 1L) "" else as.character(k)
    x[[paste0("annual_sin", suffix)]] <- sin(2 * pi * k * time / 365.25)
    x[[paste0("annual_cos", suffix)]] <- cos(2 * pi * k * time / 365.25)
  }
  x
}
```

# 4. Modelling data

Rows removed before fitting:

- dates before `fit_start`;
- each series' rows before its first sale (the store or family was not yet active).

The response is `z = log(1 + sales)`.

```{r panel}
key_all <- paste(train$store_nbr, train$family, sep = " | ")
pos <- train$sales > 0
first_sale <- tapply(as.numeric(train$date[pos]), key_all[pos], min)
start <- first_sale[key_all]
keep <- train$date >= fit_start & !is.na(start) & as.numeric(train$date) >= start
panel <- train[keep, ]
panel$key <- key_all[keep]
panel <- panel[order(panel$key, panel$date), ]
panel$z <- log1p(panel$sales)

hc <- make_holiday_calendar(stores, holidays_events,
  seq(min(panel$date), max(test$date), by = "day"))
m <- match(paste(panel$date, panel$store_nbr), paste(hc$date, hc$store_nbr))
feats <- make_features(panel$date, panel$onpromotion, hc$holiday[m], hc$workday[m])
X <- model.matrix(~ trend + weekday + promo + holiday + workday + payday15 + payday_end +
  annual_sin + annual_cos + annual_sin2 + annual_cos2, feats)[, -1]

rows_by_key <- split(seq_len(nrow(panel)), panel$key)
```

# 5. Model

For series $s$ (one store and family) on day $t$:

$$z_{s,t} = a_s + b_{g(s)}^\top x_{s,t} + n_{s,t}$$

- $a_s$: intercept, one per series in every model.
- $x_{s,t}$: trend, weekday, promotions, holiday, make-up workday, two payday flags, two annual Fourier pairs.
- $n_{s,t}$: SARIMA error, one model per series.
- $b_{g(s)}$: regression coefficients, shared within group $g$.

The three models differ only in $g$:

| Model | Coefficients shared across |
|---|---|
| `series` | nothing (one set per series) |
| `family` | all stores within a product family |
| `global` | all series |

**Stage 1.** Estimate $a_s$ and $b_g$ by least squares. Subtracting each
series' mean from $z$ and $x$ removes $a_s$, and regressing the demeaned
values within each group gives the same $b_g$ as a regression with one dummy per series.

```{r stage1}
fit_stage1 <- function(tr, pool) {
  i  <- which(tr); g <- panel$key[i]
  n  <- rowsum(rep(1, length(i)), g)[, 1]
  mx <- rowsum(X[i, ], g) / n                 # series means of the regressors
  mz <- rowsum(panel$z[i], g)[, 1] / n        # series means of z
  ig <- match(g, names(n))
  Xd <- X[i, ] - mx[ig, ]; zd <- panel$z[i] - mz[ig]
  pg <- switch(pool, series = g, family = panel$family[i], global = rep("all", length(i)))
  groups <- split(seq_along(i), pg)
  B <- t(vapply(groups, function(j) {
    b <- lm.fit(Xd[j, , drop = FALSE], zd[j])$coefficients
    b[is.na(b)] <- 0                          # regressors with no variation in this group
    b
  }, numeric(ncol(X))))
  e <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(panel))             # stage 1 residuals, aligned with panel rows
  for (p in names(groups)) {
    j <- groups[[p]]
    e[i[j]] <- zd[j] - Xd[j, , drop = FALSE] %*% B[p, ]
  }
  list(mx = mx, mz = mz, B = B, e = e, pool_of = tapply(pg, g, `[`, 1))
}
```

**Stage 2.** For each series, `auto.arima` fits a SARIMA model with weekly
period to the stage 1 residuals: $d$ and $D$ (0 or 1) by its built-in tests,
then $p, q \le 2$ and $P, Q \le 1$ by AICc. It uses all of the series'
residuals. December 25 is absent from the data each year, so those two or
three residuals are filled with `forecast::na.interp` to give a complete daily series.

**Forecast.** $\hat z = a_s + b_g^\top x + \hat n$, returned as $\max\{0, \exp(\hat z) - 1\}$.

**Fallback rules.** These follow `storesales.rmd`, applied to the modelling
data above, and are the same for all three models:

| Case | Forecast |
|---|---|
| No history, or all zeros | 0 |
| At least 365 days, at least 90% zeros, last 91 days all zero, no promotions in the forecast days | 0 |
| Fewer than 60 days, or stage 2 fails | Last observed value for each weekday |

```{r stage2}
complete_residuals <- function(e, d) {
  full <- seq(min(d), max(d), by = "day")       # every calendar day, including absent ones
  forecast::na.interp(ts(e[match(full, d)], frequency = 7))
}

weekday_naive <- function(y, d, d_new) {
  out <- rep(tail(y, 1), length(d_new))
  for (j in seq_along(d_new)) {
    v <- y[as.integer(d) %% 7L == as.integer(d_new[j]) %% 7L]
    if (length(v)) out[j] <- tail(v, 1)
  }
  out
}

forecast_series <- function(r, origin, s1) {
  d <- panel$date[r]
  i_tr <- r[d <= origin]; i_te <- r[d > origin & d <= origin + h]
  if (!length(i_te)) return(NULL)
  y <- panel$sales[i_tr]; d_tr <- panel$date[i_tr]; d_te <- panel$date[i_te]
  inactive <- length(y) >= 365 && mean(y == 0) >= 0.9 && all(tail(y, 91) == 0) &&
    all(panel$onpromotion[i_te] == 0)
  pred <- if (!length(y) || all(y == 0) || inactive) {
    rep(0, length(i_te))
  } else if (length(y) < 60) {
    weekday_naive(y, d_tr, d_te)
  } else tryCatch({
    k <- panel$key[r[1]]
    e <- complete_residuals(s1$e[i_tr], d_tr)
    fit <- forecast::auto.arima(e, max.p = 2, max.q = 2,
      max.P = 1, max.Q = 1, max.d = 1, max.D = 1, allowdrift = FALSE)
    ef <- as.numeric(forecast::forecast(fit, h = h)$mean)
    xf <- sweep(X[i_te, , drop = FALSE], 2, s1$mx[k, ])
    day <- as.integer(as.numeric(d_te) - as.numeric(origin))
    zhat <- s1$mz[[k]] + as.numeric(xf %*% s1$B[s1$pool_of[[k]], ]) + ef[day]
    pmax(0, expm1(zhat))
  }, error = function(err) weekday_naive(y, d_tr, d_te))
  data.frame(key = panel$key[i_te], family = panel$family[i_te], date = d_te,
    actual = panel$sales[i_te], pred = pred)
}
```

# 6. Holdout evaluation

The first knit fits every series under each model, which takes roughly an
hour. The results are saved to disk and reloaded on later knits.

```{r evaluate}
if (file.exists(cache)) {
  results <- readRDS(cache)
} else {
  runs <- list()
  for (p in pools) {
    s1 <- fit_stage1(panel$date <= origin, p)
    out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rows_by_key, forecast_series, origin = origin, s1 = s1))
    runs[[p]] <- data.frame(model = p, out)
    message("Finished ", p)
  }
  results <- do.call(rbind, runs)
  saveRDS(results, cache)
}
```

# 7. Results

The score is the competition metric,
$\mathrm{RMSLE} = \sqrt{\operatorname{mean}[(\log(1+\hat y) - \log(1+y))^2]}$; lower is better.

```{r results}
results$model <- factor(results$model, levels = pools)
results$sq <- (log1p(results$pred) - log1p(results$actual))^2
knitr::kable(data.frame(Model = pools, RMSLE = as.numeric(sqrt(tapply(results$sq, results$model, mean)))),
  digits = 4, caption = "Holdout RMSLE by model")
```

```{r results-by-family}
by_family <- sqrt(tapply(results$sq, list(results$family, results$model), mean))
knitr::kable(by_family[order(-by_family[, "series"]), ], digits = 3,
  caption = "Holdout RMSLE by product family")
```

These scores are not directly comparable with the Kaggle score: they exclude
series that have never sold and use different dates.
